skill.name: humanizer
skill.description: Humanizes AI-generated or AI-sounding drafts by identifying common LLM writing patterns and rewriting text in a more natural voice.
skill.summary: Rewrites AI-sounding drafts into clearer, more natural prose.
skill.author: softaworks

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from installation examples, citations, and quoted writing examples. One low-risk documentation issue remains because the README tells users to clone a remote GitHub repository directly into the Claude skills directory.

remediation.issue: README install instructions clone a remote repository directly into the Claude skills directory.
remediation.suggestion: Point installation instructions to the audited package source, or pin a verified release or commit before asking users to install it.

content.value_statement: AI-generated drafts often sound inflated, generic, or formulaic. This skill identifies common AI writing patterns and rewrites text in a clearer human voice.
actual_capabilities: Identifies common AI writing patterns, including inflated significance and vague attribution.
Rewrites promotional, formulaic, and overstructured prose into direct language.
Removes chatbot artifacts, excessive hedging, repeated em dashes, and generic conclusions.
Preserves the main meaning while adapting sentence rhythm and tone.
Can provide a brief summary of the changes made.
limitations: Does not verify facts or add citations unless source material is provided.
Does not guarantee that text will pass automated AI detection tools.
May change voice too strongly if the desired tone is not specified.
Needs context to preserve specialized terms and audience expectations.

use_cases.title: Editorial cleanup
use_cases.description: Review drafts for inflated claims, vague sourcing, and formulaic AI phrasing before publication.

use_cases.title: Product copy revision
use_cases.description: Turn generic launch copy into concrete language that explains features, benefits, and evidence clearly.

use_cases.title: Documentation polish
use_cases.description: Make generated explanations, release notes, and guides sound direct without losing technical meaning.

prompt_templates.title: Simple humanize
prompt_templates.prompt: Humanize this text while preserving the meaning and tone: [paste text]
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this for a quick rewrite of a short paragraph.

prompt_templates.title: Tone-aware rewrite
prompt_templates.prompt: Rewrite this draft so it sounds natural for [audience]. Keep the tone [formal/casual/technical] and remove obvious AI writing patterns: [paste text]
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this when the audience and tone matter.

prompt_templates.title: Pattern audit and rewrite
prompt_templates.prompt: Identify the strongest AI writing patterns in this draft, then provide a cleaner rewrite and a short change summary: [paste text]
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this when you want both diagnosis and revision.

prompt_templates.title: Advanced style preservation
prompt_templates.prompt: Revise this long draft to reduce AI-sounding language while preserving terminology, structure, claims, and source-sensitive wording. Flag any facts that need verification: [paste text]
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this for high-stakes or technical content.

output_examples.input: The update serves as a testament to our commitment to innovation and delivers a seamless, intuitive, and powerful experience.
output_examples.output: The update adds faster search, saved filters, and offline access. These changes help users finish common tasks with fewer steps.

output_examples.input: Despite challenges, the team continues to thrive and shape the evolving landscape of customer engagement.
output_examples.output: The team missed its first launch date, then reduced onboarding time by 18 percent after simplifying the setup flow.

output_examples.input: Here is a comprehensive overview of the policy. I hope this helps, and let me know if you need more details.
output_examples.output: The policy takes effect on July 1. It applies to new vendor contracts and renewals signed after that date.

best_practices: Provide the audience, desired tone, and any terms that must stay unchanged.
Include source facts when the draft contains claims that need support.
Review the final text for accuracy, voice, and compliance before publishing.
anti_patterns: Do not use the skill to hide plagiarism or misrepresent authorship.
Do not ask for a rewrite without giving context for audience and tone.
Do not accept added details unless they are supported by your sources.

faq.question: Does this skill only remove em dashes?
faq.answer: No. It also targets vague claims, inflated language, formulaic structure, chatbot artifacts, and other common AI writing patterns.

faq.question: Can it preserve a formal style?
faq.answer: Yes. Tell the model to keep a formal, technical, academic, or casual tone before the rewrite begins.

faq.question: Will it check whether the facts are true?
faq.answer: No. It improves style and clarity, but factual verification still requires sources or separate research.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, or Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Will it make text undetectable as AI-written?
faq.answer: No. It improves naturalness, but it does not guarantee any result from an AI detection tool.

faq.question: What should I provide with my draft?
faq.answer: Provide the text, audience, tone, required terminology, and any facts or citations that must remain unchanged.
